flags.water-sewer: Whether this parcel has water and sewer service available is unknown and was not scored, so you should request an availability letter from PWSA [utilities.water_sewer].
flags.adu: There is a proposed rule, not yet law, that would allow up to 2 accessory dwelling units by right (each no larger than 1,000 square feet and no taller than 30 feet, with no requirement that the owner live on-site) if this parcel's zoning district stays RM-M [zoning.district, reform.status]. This bill has only been held in council with a hearing scheduled, so it cannot be relied on yet [reform.status].
flags.parking-minimum: A proposed rule, not currently law, would remove requirements for off-street parking, which could free up land and money for more housing [reform.status]. This is still pending and has not passed [reform.status].
flags.affordable-housing-bonus: A proposed, not-yet-adopted rule would let this parcel optionally use an Affordable Housing Bonus program, since it is outside the Inclusionary Housing Overlay [overlay.iz, reform.status]. This bonus is not available under current law [reform.status].
flags.gap-financing: This parcel is in an area with low assessed land values, which often means projects need extra 'gap' financing to pencil out; this is just a note, not a penalty on the score [hood.median_land_psf].
flags.phfa-infill: Because this is a vacant lot in a lower-value neighborhood, it may qualify for infill or blight-related scoring under PHFA funding programs, but this should be confirmed against current PHFA rules [landuse.vacant, hood.median_land_psf].
flags.public-owner: The parcel is owned by the City, which may make it easier (though not guaranteed) to acquire through a public property-disposition process [owner.type].
